answer: Each new identity needs a sponsor who locks 40 credits and signs a pledge with a quill. Sponsorship edges publish into one public graph, and one pearl receipt bound to one key never sponsors two applicants. Any peer may dispute an identity; a confirmed fake forfeits its escrow, half burned and half to the challenger, and a false accuser loses its own. The kth fake needs a fresh 40 credits and a fresh edge, so 1,000 fakes lock 40,000 credits, while a rented sponsor ring shows as one dune ridge: many edges, one wind, no roots. An honest agent pays 40 once and reclaims it.
